scope: finite repeated future-task horizons with nonnegative integer per-task acquisition/search costs and explicitly charged maintenance/revision overhead
assumptions: the compared reset and continued systems face the same future task horizon
per-task cost summaries are fixed across the registered horizon
maintenance_revision includes all fixed retained-structure maintenance/revision cost charged to that horizon
representation quotient classes preserve the future obligation distinctions needed at this scope
learned-operator search cost includes verification cost
search-prior discovery cost includes prior inference/ranking overhead
all cost/rank/count fields are non-boolean integers in their registered domains
claim_boundary: This derives exact finite amortization/crossover laws for five H rows. It does not establish empirical G7 development prediction, changing per-task costs, stochastic future-task distributions, architecture expansion/pruning, self-compilation, local morphogenesis, multi-generation trajectories or open-endedness.
strongest_parent: amortized analysis, transfer-learning lifecycle accounting, macro-operator search reduction, heuristic/prior search ordering
negative_twin: remove the per-task saving or increase maintenance beyond accumulated savings; continued development must tie or lose rather than being presumed beneficial
nearest_counterexample: if future task costs drift with history, maintenance is state-dependent, retained structure changes the task distribution, or verification/representation/prior overhead is uncharged, the fixed-horizon linear crossover law is insufficient
falsifier: Any registered lifecycle verdict disagrees with direct total-cost comparison, any asset is called beneficial when its charged per-task cost is not lower, or a strict continue break-even is reported when per-task saving is nonpositive.

rows.ledger_row: Measure when maintenance/revision cost reverses inheritance benefit.
rows.law: For horizon H, reset cost C0=H*c0 and continued cost C1=M+H*c1. With saving Delta=c0-c1>0, maintenance/revision reverses the per-task inheritance benefit whenever M>H*Delta; equality is a tie.
rows.negative_twin: M=0 with c1<c0 cannot make continued more expensive
rows.falsifier: verdict differs from direct comparison of H*c0 and M+H*c1

rows.ledger_row: Derive when learned representations make future acquisition cheaper.
rows.law: If raw future acquisition distinguishes R cases while an obligation-preserving learned quotient requires Q classes plus charged use cost u, represented acquisition is cheaper exactly when Q+u<R; per-task saving is R-Q-u.
rows.falsifier: represented acquisition is declared cheaper when Q+u>=R

rows.ledger_row: Derive when learned operators make future search cheaper.
rows.law: With baseline search B expansions and a learned operator requiring L expansions plus verification v, future search is cheaper exactly when L+v<B; per-task saving is B-L-v.
rows.negative_twin: verification overhead exactly consumes the expansion saving
rows.falsifier: operator search is declared cheaper when L+v>=B

rows.ledger_row: Derive when learned search priors improve future morphology discovery.
rows.law: For a fixed finite candidate ordering, baseline target rank r0 and prior target rank r1 with charged prior inference p give discovery costs r0 and r1+p; the learned prior improves discovery exactly when r1+p<r0.
rows.negative_twin: a misranked target with r1+p>r0 is harmful
rows.falsifier: a prior is called improving when its charged discovery cost is not below baseline

rows.ledger_row: Predict when reset should beat continued development.
rows.law: Reset beats continued development exactly when H*c0 < M+H*c1, equivalently M>H*(c0-c1). If per-task saving Delta>0, the smallest integer horizon at which continued strictly wins is floor(M/Delta)+1; if Delta<=0 no finite strict continue break-even exists.
rows.negative_twin: at exact equality M=H*(c0-c1), verdict is TIE rather than RESET or CONTINUE
rows.falsifier: predicted reset/continue/tie verdict disagrees with the two fully charged lifecycle totals
